event: Elsie wakes to the bread smell; the market flower in its cup has gone soft overnight.
She waters the plants and tells Sunny the lemon that today she wants a quest with flowers in it.
She laces the halter, pins the clip, and packs salve, bandages and her notebook.
At the guild hall Tamsin is already at the F-rank notices with a finger on the moonbells.
Tamsin says the apothecary on Mortar Lane wants open moonbells by morning, and pays on delivery.

memory.fact: An apothecary pays on delivery, and the guild pays out later.
An apothecary pays on delivery, and the guild pays out later.
The moonbell notice is from the apothecary on Mortar Lane: two dozen open moonbells, by morning.

event: Elsie says her mother taught her moonbells: blue, night-blooming, brewed for fever.

memory.fact: Elsie's mother taught her moonbells: blue night-blooming flowers she brewed into fever draughts.

event: She says they open all together at dusk and shut again by midnight, so it must be night.

memory.fact: Moonbells open all together at dusk, and are shut again by midnight.
Moonbells open all together at dusk, and are shut again by midnight.
Moonbells open only between dusk and midnight, and a closed moonbell is worthless to an apothecary.

event: Tilly arrives with her apron on the right way round and asks where moonbells grow.
Tamsin says at the Glasswood's edge, an hour east of the east gate, in hollows under glass trees.

memory.fact: The Glasswood's edge is an hour's walk east of the east gate, along a cart track through meadows.
The Glasswood's edge is an hour's walk east of the east gate, along a cart track through meadows.
Moonbells grow in shady hollows at the Glasswood's edge, among the roots of the glass trees.
Moonbells grow in shady hollows at the Glasswood's edge, among the roots of the glass trees.

event: Tilly asks if the Glasswood is underground; Tamsin says it's all sky, and Tilly lights up.

memory.fact: The Glasswood is a dungeon wood of glass-barked trees out past the east gate.

event: Cora comes out of the charcoal door as the clerk enters the party for the moonbells.
Cora says she walks the Glasswood edge on patrols, and will walk it with them tonight.

memory.fact: Cora has walked the Glasswood on Wardens' patrols, and knows its edge well.

event: Tamsin says on summer nights a pack of bramblewolves hunts the edge.

memory.fact: On summer nights a pack of bramblewolves hunts the Glasswood's edge: lean, thorn-furred, lamp-eyed.

event: She says they fear fire and loud noise, and go for whoever runs.

event: Tilly goes pale, then says she can make fire and she can certainly make noise.
Elsie asks Tamsin to come and sit with her on the bench by the board.
She asks: if the red comes tonight, may she try her Tether on Tamsin?
Elsie says a Tether is a pact, and the one bound can break it whenever she likes.

memory.fact: A Tether Elsie makes is a pact the bound one can break at will.
A Tether Elsie makes is a pact the bound one can break at will.

event: Tamsin looks at her hands a long while and says she has always been alone in the red.
Then she says yes, try, and her ears go red to the tips.
Elsie turns to Cora and asks if that is enough, under the Accord.
Cora asks Tamsin to say it again in front of her; Tamsin says it again, louder.
Cora writes it in the ledger, and reads it back: leave given, Tamsin Reyes, before the guild.
Cora says the hall's business is done till the east gate, and goes to the charcoal door.
Tilly asks Elsie to help her brew flame and noise for tonight, if she doesn't mind sulphur.
Tilly's room on Pickle Row smells of sulphur and is mostly a bench of glass.
The only seat is the bed, so Elsie sits on it with her knees drawn up and watches.
Tilly brews fast and talks faster, and Elsie hands her things before she asks for them.
Tilly stops with a vial in the air and stares at Elsie, then at her own open hand.
Elsie says she watches what Tilly reaches for; Tilly goes pink and drops the stopper.
By noon there are flame vials stoppered in a row, and a fat bang-flask Tilly carries like an egg.
They eat bread and cheese on the bed, and Tilly gets crumbs in Elsie's lap and brushes them out.
Tilly's hand stops on Elsie's knee, and she takes it back as if burnt.
Tilly asks if Elsie is frightened about tonight; Elsie says a little, about the wolves.
Elsie walks home along the canal at mid-afternoon to rest before the night.
She lies in the attic with the round window open, wide awake.
She opens her window by wishing and reads the word Tether a long time.
She packs salve, bandages, bread and apples, and laces her boots tight.
The east gate stands at the east end of the south canal, with a clerk's booth beside it.
The clerk writes the party into his book, and Elsie pays him for the Glasswood licence.

changes.note: One silver lantern for the party's Glasswood licence: 100 → 90 pips

event: He says F-rank goes a mile into the wood, to the white posts, and no farther.
They walk the cart track east through meadows, with the sun going down behind them.
Tamsin walks beside Elsie and swings Margery, and is quiet for a whole field.
Tilly walks with Cora and asks her about the white posts until Cora answers her.
The Glasswood rises ahead: trees with clear glass bark, chiming in the evening wind.
Elsie stops on the track with her mouth open, and Tilly takes her hand to see what she sees.
Tamsin leads them along the edge to a shady hollow among the glass roots.
The moonbells lie shut and blue among the roots, a whole hollow of them.
They sit on the hollow's lip and eat apples while the light goes.
At dusk the moonbells open all together, and the hollow turns pale blue.
Elsie says that is exactly how her mother described it, and her eyes fill.
Glass-winged moths drift up out of the trees; Cora says they are glimmer moths and harmless.
Elsie picks with her fingers among the roots and slices a fingertip on fallen glass.
Tamsin says fallen glass cuts like a knife, and gatherers here wear full gloves.
She unwinds one of her own knuckle wraps and binds Elsie's fingers in it, slow.
Elsie thanks her and Tamsin keeps hold of her hand a moment longer than the binding needs.
They gather in the bells' own pale glow, Elsie choosing full-open bells and Tilly counting aloud.
Cora stands at the hollow's edge facing the wood, ledger shut, watching the trees.
A thornhare bolts from the roots and Tilly yelps; Tamsin says it bites only if cornered.
By half past eight Tamsin, who read the notice, says they have all it asks for, and a few to spare.
Lamp-eyed shapes stand up between the glass trunks, lean and thorn-furred.
Tamsin says, quiet, bramblewolves; stand still, all of you.
Tilly's feet start to turn; Elsie takes her hand hard and holds her where she stands.
Tilly lights a flame vial and throws it, and fire runs along the leaf litter.
The pack circles wide of the fire, and one comes round at Tilly's open side.
Tamsin steps across it with Margery; the wolf's teeth catch her forearm.
Tamsin's eyes go flat, all at once, and the red has her.
She throws the wolf off and turns with the axe up, and Elsie is the nearest thing to her.
Elsie stands her ground; she reaches for Tamsin, and asks for her Tether.
A window opens in the dark above them: Tether.
A thread of light runs from Elsie's chest to Tamsin's, thin as a hair and warm.
Tamsin stops with the axe high; her flat eyes find Elsie through the red.
She turns her back on her party, and sets herself between them and the wolves.
Inside the red she fights only wolves, and keeps the axe clear of her own.
Tilly throws the bang-flask; the noise cracks the glass trees and they ring like bells.
The pack breaks at the fire and the noise and runs into the wood.
Tamsin stands swinging at nothing until the red burns out, and then she drops to her knees.
Elsie feels an ache in her own forearm that is not hers, and knows where Tamsin is hurt.
She kneels and finds the wolf bite on Tamsin's forearm, exactly where the ache is.
Tamsin says she heard Elsie in there, in the red, the whole time.
Elsie says she can break the Tether whenever she likes; Tamsin says, leave it.
Cora opens her ledger by Tilly's flame and writes, and reads it aloud to Elsie.
Skills used: Tether, on Tamsin Reyes, by her leave, given before the guild.
Then Cora writes another line, and turns the page before Elsie can see it.
In the empty ranger's hut at the edge, Elsie cleans and bandages Tamsin's arm.
Tilly sits pressed against Elsie's other side and keeps hold of her sleeve.
Elsie opens her own window, and under Tether it reads a name now: Tamsin.
They walk the cart track back under the stars, the moonbells glowing in the satchel.
Tamsin walks so close to Elsie that their arms touch the whole way, and both let them.
At the east gate the clerk writes the party out of his book.
The apothecary on Mortar Lane opens in her nightcap and counts the open bells.
She pays on the step, and Elsie, Tamsin and Tilly each pocket a third.

event: A window opens over the step: Level up, and under Tether a new skill, Hold.
Cora says she is off duty, and stands a moment, and goes up the lane alone.
Tilly hugs Elsie, then Tamsin, then runs for Pickle Row with her braids flying.
Tamsin walks Elsie to the Honeycomb door and says goodnight twice.
Elsie says she loves her, and Tamsin stands very still on the step.
In the attic Elsie unwinds Tamsin's knuckle wrap from her finger and lays it on the sill.
